title: Amos and Andy and divisions over black image
summary: Tex says he liked Amos and Andy and criticizes the NAACP and Urban League for wanting it off the air.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I have a note on how does when blacks first started coming on TV I mean films stuff like Amos and Andy what was your reaction
to things like Amos and Andy

TV? I guess like I used to like this show because I thought it was funny. I didn't have a great affinity to try to take it off the air but you had the NAACP and the Urban League and a certain element of people who had gravitated to schools and colleges and say well we kind of cultured now we don't need them kind of people no more. Well I don't feel that we could throw those people out because they still are part of the entertainment history of this nation and I think they should be seen and they should be heard because you see the thing about it what the NAACP and the Urban League was talking about and those who followed that perception was that we don't want to be identified with those kind of people but then again I said remember these people are still a child of God and they are making money when some of the people who don't like them you understand what I'm saying that they are part of the arts and television and entertainment programs are part of the arts it may not be the culture art that a lot of people think it should be because certain members of the NAACP or the Urban League or the ilk whoever wanted to follow that direction to say well we don't want to identify with them but we would rather identify with Mahalia Jackson or somebody else and then we got an element of blanks who didn't want to be identified with Mahalia Jackson you take a certain element of the Catholic group and Lord forgive me talking because you got an element today in the black community where we have the Knights of Columbus which was founded basically by white folks then we have the Knights of Peter Claver which is followed by black folks now that's a division in the Catholic Church you understand they're two different type of organizations but we're still talking about the same God the same Jesus and the same Catholic Church case closed
